record.paper_title: New results and open questions for SIR-PH epidemic models with linear birth rate, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease and vaccination fatalities
record.context_brief: Scaled model as perturbation of the first approximation
record.original_question: Can the scaled epidemic model with linear births and disease-induced fatalities be rigorously analyzed as a perturbation of the first approximation model, for example using slow-fast, singular-perturbation, or homogenization techniques, so that conclusions about endemic equilibria and stability can transfer from the approximation to the scaled model?

evidence.quote:
The well-studied classic
models may then be recovered via a heuristic "first approximation" (FA) of ignoring the extra
terms. This approximation, which deserves being investigated rigorously via slow-fast/singular
perturbation/homogeneization techniques, has the merit of putting under one umbrella constant
and varying population models with linear birth rates.
Study the scaled model as a perturbation of the FA model.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a compartmental SIR-type epidemic model with linear birth rate, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease- and vaccination-induced fatalities, whose total population N(t) is not constant. Concretely, let the state be a vector (S, I, R) (or, more generally, (S, \mathbf{I}, R) with a phase-type infectious compartment \mathbf{I} \in \mathbb{R}_+^n) evolving according to a system of ODEs of the form

  S' = \Lambda - \beta(N) S \mathbf{e}^\top \mathbf{I} - (\mu + \nu) S + \gamma R,
  \mathbf{I}' = (\beta(N) S \mathbf{e}^\top \mathbf{I}) \mathbf{a} + A \mathbf{I} - \mu \mathbf{I},
  R' = \mathbf{b}^\top \mathbf{I} + \nu S - (\mu + \gamma) R,

where \Lambda>0 is a constant birth (recruitment) rate, \mu>0 the natural death rate, \nu \ge 0 the vaccination rate, \gamma \ge 0 the loss-of-immunity rate, \mathbf{a} \in \mathbb{R}_+^n a probability vector, A a sub-generator matrix and \mathbf{b} = -(A+ \text{diag}(\text{death rates}))\mathbf{1} the recovery-rate vector, and where disease-induced and vaccination-induced fatalities cause N = S + \mathbf{e}^\top \mathbf{I} + R to be non-constant. Rescale this "full scaled model" by setting s = S/N, \mathbf{i} = \mathbf{I}/N, r = R/N, and let (\mathcal{S}) denote the resulting ODE system in the simplex variables.

The "first approximation" (FA) model (\mathcal{S}_0) is obtained from (\mathcal{S}) by dropping the additional terms in (\mathcal{S}) that arise from disease/vaccination fatalities and from the non-constancy of N — recovering a classical fixed-population SIR-PH-type system whose endemic equilibria and their local/global stability are well understood in terms of a basic reproduction number R_0.

Problem: Develop a rigorous perturbation theory that realizes (\mathcal{S}) as a small perturbation of (\mathcal{S}_0), using slow-fast / geometric singular perturbation theory, averaging, or homogenization methods, identifying a natural small parameter \varepsilon (e.g. encoding the ratio of fatality and demographic rates to the dominant epidemic timescales) such that (\mathcal{S}_\varepsilon) \to (\mathcal{S}_0) as \varepsilon \to 0. Using such a framework, prove that for sufficiently small \varepsilon:

(i) every hyperbolic endemic equilibrium of the FA model (\mathcal{S}_0) persists as a nearby equilibrium of the scaled model (\mathcal{S}_\varepsilon), with the same local stability type;
(ii) the basic reproduction number, endemic equilibrium coordinates, and Lyapunov/stability conclusions for (\mathcal{S}_0) transfer to (\mathcal{S}_\varepsilon) with quantitative O(\varepsilon) error bounds;
(iii) global asymptotic stability properties (where available for (\mathcal{S}_0)) are inherited by (\mathcal{S}_\varepsilon) on appropriate invariant regions.

Determine to what extent such a rigorous reduction is possible, and identify the precise hypotheses on the parameters under which the transfer of endemic-equilibrium existence and stability from the FA model to the scaled model can be justified.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open direction for future work: to rigorously justify the heuristic "first approximation" reduction for scaled SIR-PH models with linear births and fatalities via singular-perturbation/homogenization methods. No subsequent work establishing such a rigorous perturbation analysis for this class of models was located.
